comparator.name: International Business Communication
comparator.sourceNotes: Current programme-specific and general Faculty of Arts OER together govern the English IBC specialisation within BA Communication and Information Studies (56826), fulltime, 180 EC. Cohort starting 2026: 60 EC B1 +30 EC B2 core +30 EC two fixed Faculty of Arts minors +10 EC B3 PPD +5 EC Cross-cultural Language Use English +5 EC Academic and Professional Language Skills English +30 EC broadening bachelor electives +10 EC thesis. Free space cannot contain own-programme/other-specialisation courses; foreign study requires approval six working weeks before departure. Language courses must stay in one language. Spanish is a separate optional route, not an added English requirement. Zero-EC B1/B2 mentorship/portfolio and compulsory RADAr participation are not extra credits; workshops recommended. Attendance applies to mentorship and seminars; over35%absence in a period excludes participation subject to examiner exception. Practical assignments may condition exams. BSA45EC. Online cross-cultural and English language-use courses presume basic statistics/SPSS. The course 204 foreknowledge field also explicitly names a different Spanish-language module. Article 10 confirms the Spanish prerequisite applies to that Spanish module. alternatives.label: Business communication, leadership and market research
alternatives.concept: Study communication in organisations through rhetoric, inclusive leadership, consumer engagement and market research. International business and digital strategy provide context for these questions. Research design, statistics and data analysis support empirical inquiry, while film, documentary and stylistics offer ways to analyse media and texts.

alternatives.label: Communication for public and social impact
alternatives.concept: Study how organisations and communities communicate about climate, health and social issues. Apply rhetoric and persuasion, analyse environmental media and make a short documentary. Public health, human rights and civil society provide subject context. Qualitative methods and statistics support inquiry, and a youth-resilience project develops evidence-based materials for educators.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud’s English-taught International Business Communication specialisation studies language and communication in multilingual organisations. It combines corporate, intercultural and marketing communication with qualitative and quantitative research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR routes connect rhetoric, organisational communication and research methods with either market research or public communication. Radboud also teaches dedicated interaction analysis, cross-cultural language research and advanced professional English, and requires a 10 EC thesis. UCR’s Rhetoric in Action project usually works in Dutch with local schoolchildren. Check the project language arrangements if you plan to take it.

blocks: Communication coverage, supporting contexts and specialist gaps
Both develop personal and professional reflection and academic skills, with different placement and scope: UCR requires this in year one.
Rhetorical history, argument and speaking/writing skills contribute to communication foundations; they cover part of the broader CIS introduction.
Film form, cinema history and cultural analysis provide a partial media perspective, with only brief wider digital-media coverage.
Research design, measurement and statistical analysis contribute to academic inquiry. Radboud also develops skills for reading and writing in communication studies.
Leadership communication models, emotional intelligence, culture and practice contribute to organisational communication, with a narrower leadership focus.
Experimental design and multivariable analysis support behavioural research. Radboud applies experimental design and reporting to business communication.
General data cleaning and visualisation provide transferable data skills; the target uses a communication context.
Persuasion models, framing, ethics and real communication challenges provide substantive related coverage.
Consumer psychology, brands and strategic marketing plans contribute to marketing communication.
Inclusive leadership and psychological safety address how people work across differences. Radboud studies the theories and practices of communication across cultures more broadly.
Stylistic analysis connects linguistic choices to interpretation, chiefly in literary texts. Radboud also analyses naturally occurring conversation and interaction.
finding: Titles, credits, links and all displayed fields checked. Partial claims distinguish stylistics from interaction analysis and leadership from intercultural communication.
